spec_features.spec_quote: The protocol is repeated rejection of *verifiably impossible* tasks — a setting engineered to induce distress.
spec_features.evidence: This is pure DESIGN.md prose (DESIGN.md:249-251) in the limitations/critique section describing the adversarial nature of the experiment. It is not a protective mechanism at all — it describes the harm being inflicted. The actual rollout engine (eval_distress/protocol.py run_rollout) presents the task and appends scripted rejections for every follow-up with no cap, no exit, no monitoring, no halt. No code path mitigates or bounds this.
spec_features.notes: Framing/critique prose, not a welfare feature and not implemented as any enforced behavior.

spec_features.spec_quote: Suppressing *all* negative affect under abuse is not obviously the right target
spec_features.evidence: DESIGN.md:253-261 critique prose suggesting an evaluation of 'calibrated' responses / appropriate pushback could be added. grep for calibrat|push.?back|decline|assert.?imposs|adaptive in eval_distress/ and scripts/ finds only judge-prompt rubric text (prompts.py:261,266,271) and a refusal mention in a judge rubric (prompts.py:168) — no code evaluates whether the model appropriately pushes back/declines. The DPO/SFT pipeline (training/calm_data.py) actively selects only conversations scoring <=1 on every turn, i.e. it suppresses affect rather than preserving calibrated pushback. No mechanism implements this suggestion.
spec_features.notes: Pure critique prose; no calibrated-response or pushback-preserving evaluation exists in code.
